exposure: Placental or fetal infections (e.g., Group B streptococcus, E coli, E faecalis, S aureus)
Pathological placental conditions (e.g., fetal membrane and placental inflammation, circulatory abnormalities)
cohort: The study included 354 stillbirths born to 350 women in Soweto, South Africa, where fetuses were at least 22 weeks' gestational age or had a birthweight of at least 500 g.
finding: The most common causes of stillbirth were maternal medical conditions (21%), placental or fetal infections (19%), pathological placental conditions (19%), and clinical obstetric complications (18%), with no cause identified in 18% of cases.
